headline: Sequence-based models predict enzyme activity using benchmarks and prior knowledge
label: Sequence Based Enzyme Function Prediction
summary: Negative-inclusive benchmarks and ontology-informed pre-training are emerging to test and improve sequence-based enzyme and metabolite function predictors.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of curated, structured biological information to predict enzyme or molecule function from sequence or chemical representation. MCDBench provides 792 medium-chain dehydrogenase enzyme-substrate-cofactor combinations, including validated inactives, to benchmark predictors with negative cases included. CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from protein sequence alone using learnable dual-descriptor weights and reports improved regression and classification. PhageLysClass applies ESM2 protein language model embeddings with a hierarchical classifier to recognize phage lytic proteins and separate endolysins. The published ontology pre-training study embeds bio-ontology hierarchy knowledge into deep learning as an intermediate step, improving metabolite property prediction. What is new is the emphasis on negative-inclusive evaluation and prior-knowledge integration. The lightweight CNN separating coding from intergenomic DNA is a looser fit, sharing only the sequence-model approach.
